resources.string: How to measure
The reference stick
The reference stick is a flat ruler with red and white stripes. You know its length, so the app can turn what it sees in the photo into real sizes.
Lay the stick flat on the same surface as the object you want to measure.
Before you start, enter the stick\'s real length and width in Settings (the gear button on the camera screen).
Keep the stick flat against that surface. Do not prop it up.
If your stick has a border, include the border when you enter its length and width, and when you place the red box.
Take the photo
Frame the object and the stick together, then tap Capture.
Shoot at a moderate angle. Straight on is fine, but avoid nearly edge-on views, where you see the surface almost from the side.
Keep all four corners of the object and the whole stick in view.
Good light and a steady hand give better results.
Mark the object and the stick
After you take the photo, two boxes appear on it.
The green box, labelled Object, is for the object. Drag its four corners onto the four corners of the object.
The red box, labelled Stick, is for the stick. The app tries to find the stick and place this box itself. Check that it outlines the stick, and drag its corners if it does not.
Drag a corner to move it. A magnifier appears while you drag, so that you can place the corner precisely.
Use two fingers to zoom in or to move the photo, so that you can reach tight corners.
If you see a Surface choice (Wall or Floor), pick what you are measuring. The app often works this out from how you held the phone.
Tap Measure when both boxes are in place. Reset puts the boxes back where they started. Retake goes back to the camera.
Settings
Before your first measurement, open Settings (the gear button) and check these:
Reference stick length: the full length of the stick, from end to end, including any border.
Reference stick width: the short side of the stick, including any border.
Display units: metres, centimetres, or feet and inches. You can change this at any time. For feet, type sizes as decimals: 1.5 means 1 foot 6 inches.
The app remembers your choices the next time you open it.
Read the result
After you tap Measure, the Measurements screen shows:
Width, Height, Area and Diagonal, in the unit you chose.
Corner angles. A corner of exactly 90° is square, so these show whether the object really is a rectangle.
Confidence: High at 70 percent or more, Medium from 40 percent to just below 70, and Low below 40 percent. The percentage does not guarantee that the size is right.
Method. This line appears only when the app used your phone\'s tilt sensor instead of the shape of the corners (the rectangle method). Check the confidence and the notes.
Notes under the result explain issues such as a steep camera angle, estimated lens details or a missing tilt reading.
Re-mark takes you back to adjust the boxes. Export shares the photo with the numbers on it. New starts again with a new photo.
Tips and accuracy
Accuracy varies with the phone, the photo and how carefully you place the stick and the corners. Check important sizes with a ruler or tape.
Everything you measure must lie flat on the same surface as the stick. Raised edges and curved surfaces give wrong results.
Avoid shadows across the stick. The app finds the stripes by their contrast.
If Confidence is Low, try another angle, or put the stick closer to the object.
The stick itself is not part of the measured size.
